title: The illusion of consciousness | Dan Dennett
summary: Philosopher Dan Dennett argues in a TED talk that we do not understand our own consciousness and that our brains often fool us. He uses perceptual examples, including a painting that invites the viewer to fill in detail.
why: HN recommends it as a short route to Dennett's view of consciousness as a bag of tricks, often in AI and cognition threads.

quote.text: I recommend the TED talk or the Google talk where he highlights this example as a way to gain insight into what consciousness may be.
